rationale: B wins because it has discipline A only performs in places: it turns the same facts into four distinct beat-ready stories without dragging in unsupported incumbents. A's "Perplexity Moves Into Commerce, Putting AI Search Directly Against Google Shopping and Amazon" is a shiny shortcut with no supplied competitor fact; B's "Perplexity now earns a fee when you buy what it recommends" finds the sharper trust story hiding inside the referral-fee fact. Both sets have useful bones, but B gives a founder less cleanup before pitching.
gaps_in_A: "Putting AI Search Directly Against Google Shopping and Amazon" invents a competitor frame the update never supplies. You can infer commerce pressure; you cannot pitch named incumbents as the story without evidence.

"for the first time, an AI search product is inserting itself into the transaction" is an unsupported category claim. That is the kind of sentence a reporter will fact-check and quietly resent you for.
"publishers and their legal teams will need to respond publicly" overstates the update. No named publisher, lawsuit posture, or public-response obligation is in the facts.
"publisher participation appears opt-in; content is cited regardless" smuggles in mechanics the update does not give. The opacity angle is strong enough without decorating it.
gaps_in_B: "takes a referral fee on every sale" is too absolute. The facts support referral fees on purchases through the in-app shopping flow, not every sale or every recommendation.
"Merchants deciding whether to list will want the terms this week" assumes merchant-listing mechanics that are not in the update. Keep it as proof to obtain, not a stated market behavior.
"first structural answer to that fight" and "first concrete monetization signal since the raise" may be true, but "first" is not in the supplied facts. That word likes to start fires.

The set could flag the self-reported nature of "hundreds of millions of queries" inside the commerce and monetization angles, not only in the uncomfortable questions. Scale claims need a collar on them.
